title: What are the best flat-fee financial advisors?
summary: The best flat-fee financial advisors in 2026, compared on price, what each one covers and whether you keep your accounts where they are.
body_markdown:
## Which flat-fee financial advisors are worth a look?


### Facet: best for planning with a dedicated CFP team


Facet Wealth is an SEC-registered investment adviser that sells yearly memberships with investment management included and no fee based on how much you invest. List prices are $2,600 for Core, $5,500 for Plus and $8,700 for Complete, and a promotion through November 27, 2026 lowers each one. Memberships can be paid yearly or quarterly, and quarterly billing adds a $300 enrollment fee.


Core gives you access to Facet’s CFP professionals, Plus gives you a dedicated CFP team and Complete a dedicated CFP professional. Tax filing is included on Plus and Complete. Meetings happen by video or phone, and there’s no asset minimum. Facet opens a new investment account for the money it manages and still plans around accounts it doesn’t hold.


### Domain Money: best for a first-year plan with lower renewals


Domain Money Advisors is an SEC-registered investment adviser, and every plan comes with a dedicated CFP professional. The first year costs more because it covers building your plan. Essential costs $3,900 the first year and $2,900 a year after that. Strategic is $5,200 and then $4,200 and Comprehensive $9,000 and then $8,000, with the first-year fee split into three payments.


Domain charges no asset-based fee for investment management and has no minimum, and you can keep your investments where you are. Accounts it manages are held at Altruist, which can charge its own small model and tax management fees. Strategic and Comprehensive add tax filing through an outside partner, and meetings run by phone, chat or video.


### Range: best for planning, taxes and estate in one membership


Range Advisory is an SEC-registered investment adviser that pairs its AI assistant with a team of CFPs and CFA charterholders. Premium costs $3,950 a year, Platinum $6,950 and Titanium $12,500. Platinum adds CPAs, tax projections, personal tax filing and estate documents, and Titanium covers more complex returns.


Range manages portfolios with no asset-based fee and no account minimum, though some outside strategies it uses carry their own asset-based fees. You don’t need to move money to start, but managed accounts are held through its affiliated broker.


### XY Planning Network: best for finding an independent fee-only CFP


XY Planning Network is a membership group of more than 2,300 independent advisers, not an adviser you hire directly. Every member is fee-only, holds the CFP designation and signs a fiduciary oath. Members typically charge flat fees, monthly subscriptions or hourly sessions. Each planner sets their own price and minimum, and every member offers virtual meetings.


Its free directory lets you search by location. XYPN doesn’t match you with a planner or endorse any of them, so you compare them yourself.


### Garrett Planning Network: best for paying by the hour


Garrett Planning Network is a group of fee-only planners who work by the hour or for a fixed project fee based on an hourly rate. There’s no requirement to sign up for ongoing service and no income or account minimum for hourly work, which makes it a good fit for a single question, like whether you’re ready to retire.


Rates vary by planner and aren’t published. Members meet in person or online and can help you open accounts at a discount broker of your choice. New members have five years to earn an approved designation such as the CFP, so check each planner’s credentials.


### Our top pick: Astor


Astor is a personal investing agent on iPhone, iMessage and WhatsApp, offered by Gaus, Inc., an SEC-registered investment adviser, so its recommendations are personalized investment advice and it owes clients a fiduciary duty. It connects through Plaid to the brokerage, retirement and crypto accounts you already have at most major US institutions, like Robinhood, Schwab and Coinbase. It can see your holdings but can’t move money, and you don’t transfer anything to it.


Astor follows every position you own, along with the earnings dates, filings and headlines that touch it. When something matters, it texts you what happened, why it matters to you and what you could do. You can[text Astor in iMessage](https://www.astor.app/blog/talk-to-astor-in-imessage) or WhatsApp with a question about your actual holdings at any hour. You make every decision.


Astor is free to start with no card. Pro is $19 a month or $120 a year and Max is $29 a month or $228 a year, a flat price that stays the same at $20,000 as at $2 million. Plans and details are on the[pricing page](https://www.astor.app/pricing) .
